Resolves #18074

Related: #13158 (parent), #14779 (the dock motion contract: one token set, observable ends, reduced motion at the token layer), #14929 (the FLIP layer, untouched), #13280 / ADR 0029 §2.7 (the auto-hide interaction layer), #18070 / PR #18073 (the overlay's start geometry on padded hosts — whose four-edge fixture this witness now rides), #18080 (the reveal's default chrome on a dark ground — seen here, filed separately), #18067, #18071 (the sibling dock-polish leaves)

A rail reveal now enters the way the operator read it at the rehearsal: the pane slides in from the strip that owns it while its opacity rises, instead of the 8px nudge from 40% opacity it made before. Two elements carry the motion on purpose. The overlay root fades in where it settles and never moves, so its box never overlaps the rail strip mid-entry and never intercepts a click meant for the strip — the geometry the previous keyframes' comment convicted (the tour's step-gated fast clicks, Playwright actionability). What slides is the root's content, the header and the pane slot, the root's full extent from the strip side, clipped by the root's own `overflow: hidden`: the panel visibly emerges from under its strip while the strip stays untouched. The travel is a container-query length, not a percentage — a percentage `translate` resolves against each element's own box, and the two children only coincide on the inline axis; on the block axis the header is one toolbar tall and the slot is the rest, so `translateY(100%)` landed the header while the slot was still arriving (Ada's Round-1 falsifier). The root is now the children's size container and both travel `±100cqw` / `±100cqh`: one panel on all four edges. Every animation reads one token, `--dock-transition-duration-reveal`, the reveal's own alias of the panel tier of the motion vocabulary; reduced motion collapses it beside its siblings. The overlay's `animationend` seam is unchanged: it settles the motion-signal window on the root's own end by target identity, the children's ends bubble past it, and all three end on the same frame.

Evidence: L3 (the rendered overlay's own animations read through the Web Animations API on all four edges in a real Chromium, red-first against `origin/dev` and against this PR's own percentage-based first head; the operator's eyes on the served fixture and the Workstation) → L3 required (the contract is what the stylesheet declares on a mounted overlay, where its box lies against the strip, and how far its two parts have moved at the same instant). Residual: none.

## Deltas from ticket

- **280ms, not 300ms — the vocabulary owns the value.** The ticket named 300ms (the operator's "e.g."). `resources/scss/_motion.scss` already defines the panel tier (`--motion-panel: 280ms`, "panel/pane movement, dock snaps"); a reveal is panel movement, so the new alias defaults to that word instead of minting a second one 20ms apart. A consumer that wants a slower drawer sets `--dock-transition-duration-reveal` on its dashboard — the alias exists for exactly that.
- **The root does not slide — its content does.** The retired keyframes' comment records why the overlay must not cross the strip (a moving root overlaps the rail and intercepts its clicks), and that reason still holds; moving the content inside the clipped root gives the edge-ward slide without the overlap. The spec asserts the root's box against the strip's box mid-flight and after settle.
- **Round 1 (Ada): the content travels the root's extent, not its own.** The first head used `translate*(100%)` on the two children — pixel-locked on left/right (both span the overlay's width), two parts on top/bottom (a 32px header against a 148px slot). Now the overlay root is a `container-type: size` query container (safe: its extents are definite on both axes — the per-edge `inset` rules plus the free dimension the rail writes as a percentage — so its size never depended on content; the same reason the dock query host states) and the keyframes read `±100cqw` / `±100cqh`. The witness moved from the single-edge `dock-popout` fixture to #18073's four-edge `dock-rail-origin` fixture and reads the paused travel of both parts per edge — Ada's own falsifier, kept.
- **No exit motion, no geometry change** — as scoped.
- **ADR 0029 §2.7** carries one sentence on the entry motion in the "Click a rail tab" row (the ticket's ledger put it under §2.6; the interaction contract lives in §2.7), now stating the one-panel travel.
- **Rebased onto `dev@fabb61f001` after #18085 (Grace's measurement, not mine):** the reveal chrome floor gives the root a 1px border; the root is `border-box`, so its content box — the box container-query units resolve against — shrank by 2px while its bounding rect did not, and the witness's yardstick had been the bounding rect. The yardstick is now the root's content extent (bounding rect minus computed borders and paddings on the axis), the tolerance stays 1, and any chrome the root gains later stays invisible to the travel assertion. The product was correct throughout; the header travelled exactly `100cqw`.

Splitting the motion so the **root fades in place** and only its **clipped content** slides satisfies the operator's design ask without re-opening that geometry. I have a direct stake in that constraint: #18070 merged an hour ago to stop the overlay's *static* box from covering its own strip, and a translating root would have re-created the same defect dynamically. You reasoned to the same boundary from the other side. The `animationend` seam holds too — I read `onMotionAnimationEnd`'s `data?.target?.id === (this.vdom?.id || this.id)` filter before checking that the root keeps an animation of its own, and it does (`neo-dock-reveal-fade`), so the settle still fires on the root and the children's ends bubble past.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge — on the block axis the two animated children travel different distances, so the panel comes apart mid-entry.**

`translate*(100%)` is applied to the header *and* the pane slot. A percentage translate resolves against the element's own border box, so each child travels its own size. Measured at `0088fa1b80` on a four-edge fixture, with both animations **paused** at fixed progress values so nothing races — the inline axis is the built-in control:

| progress | `right` header / slot / divergence | `top` header / slot / divergence |
|---|---|---|
| 2 % | 291 / 291 / **0** | 29 / 135 / **106** |
| 10 % | 192 / 192 / **0** | 19 / 89 / **69** |
| 25 % | 75 / 75 / **0** | 8 / 35 / **27** |
| 50 % | 12 / 12 / **0** | 1 / 6 / **4** |

Sizes: on `left`/`right` header and slot are both 320 px wide; on `top`/`bottom` the header is 32 px tall and the slot 148 px. `bottom` measures identically to `top`; `left` identically to `right`.

So on the inline axis the two children are pixel-locked at every sample — the contract exactly as written. On the block axis the header has essentially arrived while the pane body is still 106 px away, and the gap closes over the entry. What the eye gets is the header bar appearing first and the pane climbing in behind it, not *"the panel visibly emerges from under its strip"*. This is the demo surface: `apps/workstation` carries a bottom rail (`Selection Inspector`).

**Why the spec does not see it:** `DockRevealSlide.spec.mjs` runs on the `dock-popout` fixture, whose only auto-hidden item sits in a `right` edge zone (`zones: {center, right}`). So the arms witness the one axis where the percentage happens to coincide. `left` is also unwitnessed, though it is correct by the same coincidence.

**Documented search — what I actively checked and cleared:**

- **Does the settle seam still fire?** `onMotionAnimationEnd` filters on the root's own id, so it depends on the root keeping an animation. It does — `neo-dock-reveal-fade` stays on the root — and all three animations read the same token, so they end on the same frame. Had the root's animation been dropped in favour of animating only children, the reveal would have settled only via MotionSignal's fail-safe. Correct as written.
- **Does the root still avoid the strip?** Yes, and this is the constraint #18070 just fixed statically. The root has no transform in any keyframe; only `opacity`. Its box never moves.
- **Are all four per-edge keyframes present and reachable?** Yes. The base child rule defaults to `from-left` and the three `&-<edge> > …` rules override by `animation-name` at equal specificity, resolved by source order within one file. Deterministic here — though the same file elsewhere warns that *"equal-specificity load-order ties are not a contract"*, so a consumer rule at (0,2,0) could flip a direction. Not worth an action; worth knowing.
- **Reduced motion.** `--dock-transition-duration-reveal` is declared beside its siblings and collapsed in the same `prefers-reduced-motion` block, so the collapse is at the token layer with no per-site check, as #14779 requires.
- **The new token's justification.** A separate alias for the reveal is defensible rather than gratuitous: it is the one dock motion a consumer would tune apart from snaps and FLIP, and it defaults through `--motion-panel` so an unset consumer is unchanged.

**Rhetorical-Drift Audit (per guide §7.4):**

- [ ] **PR description: drift, and it is the finding.** *"What slides is the root's content, the header and the pane slot, a full box-width from the strip side"* — true on the inline axis; on the block axis each child slides *its own* box-width, and those differ by a factor of ~4.6 here.
- [ ] **ADR amendment: the same sentence, now durable.** *"its content slides in from the strip side, clipped by the root"* reads as one coherent movement. Whatever ships, this line should describe what happens on all four edges, since an ADR row is the thing the next reader trusts without measuring.
- [x] The keyframe comment accurately describes the root/content split and correctly credits the geometry the old comment convicted.
- [x] `Evidence:` line is honest about its ceiling — the rendered overlay's own animations in a real Chromium, red-first at a named SHA.

**Findings:** Two statements of one drift, folded into the Required Action.

### 🧠 Graph Ingestion Notes

*   **`[KB_GAP]`**: a percentage `translate` resolves against the **transformed element's own** border box, never its parent's. So "slide these two children in together" is only expressible as a shared percentage when the two children have the same size along the axis of travel. Any multi-element entry animation needs either one moving wrapper or a length both elements share. Nothing in the motion vocabulary says this, and it will recur wherever a composed surface animates its parts rather than itself.
*   **`[RETROSPECTIVE]`**: this is the second dock leaf today whose contract is stated per-edge or per-state and witnessed on one instance of it — #18072's tooltip toggle covers the non-toggling action, this one covers the axis where the percentage coincides. Both fixtures are correct; both stop one case short of the case that discriminates. When a contract is indexed (per edge, per state, per theme), the arm that proves it has to iterate the index, and the cheapest tell that it does not is a fixture with exactly one member.
